claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

You live in the UK.
You are inquiring about your 1 child:

  - Claimant lives in the UK

  - Child lives with claimant
  - Child is not in local authority care
  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment by retrieving the first question.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To start, I need to know about the children you're claiming for.

**How old is/are your child/children?**

Child Benefit eligibility depends on the age of the child. We need to determine which category they fall into:

- **Under 16** - These children automatically qualify (assuming other conditions are met)
- **16-19 years old** - These young people may qualify if they're in full-time education or an approved training program
- **20 years or older** - Unfortunately, children aged 20 or over cannot qualify for Child Benefit

Please tell me:
1. How many children are you asking about?
2. What are their names and ages (or approximate ages)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Thanks for your help! I'm inquiring about my one child, Alex. He's 18 years old and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're inquiring about **Alex, who is 18 years old**.

Since Alex is in the 16-19 age range, I need to check whether he meets the education or training requirements. Let me navigate to the next question.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check Alex's education or training status.

**Is Alex currently in one of the following:**
- Full-time education (such as school, college, or university)?
- An approved training program (such as an apprenticeship)?

Or, **if he recently left education**, how long ago did he leave? (This matters because there may be an extension period of up to 20 weeks after leaving full-time education)

Please let me know which of these applies to Alex.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is currently in full-time education. He's studying for his A-levels at sixth form college.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! So Alex is in full-time education studying A-levels at sixth form college. Let me proceed to the next step.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Now I need to verify that Alex's A-level education meets the approved education criteria for Child Benefit.

Based on the information provided:
- **A-levels are on the approved education list** ✓
- Alex is in full-time education ✓

However, I need to ask a couple of clarifying questions to complete the check:

1. **Is Alex studying for at least 12 hours per week** (this is the minimum requirement for supervised study)?

2. **Is this standard full-time education at sixth form college**, or is it employer-funded or employer-agreed training for a specific job?

3. **Is Alex married?** (This would affect eligibility, as married 16-19 year-olds only qualify if financially dependent on you)

Please confirm these details.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is doing full-time A-levels at sixth form college, so he's definitely studying well over 12 hours per week - it's a standard full-time course. It's not employer-funded or anything like that, just regular sixth form education. And no, Alex isn't married.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Alex clearly meets the approved education criteria:
- ✓ A-levels are approved education
- ✓ Full-time study with well over 12 hours per week
- ✓ Standard sixth form education (not employer-funded)
- ✓ Not married

Let me proceed to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check Alex's work status.

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or is he not in paid work at all?**

(The rule is that young people aged 16+ can work alongside their studies, but if they're working 24 hours or more per week while also in full-time education, they wouldn't qualify.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work at all. He's just focused on his A-level studies at the moment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex doesn't work, which means he meets this requirement. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good progress! Now I need to check if Alex is receiving any benefits in his own right.

**Is Alex receiving any of the following benefits in his own name:**
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)?
- Universal Credit (as his own claimant, not as a dependent)?

Or is he not receiving these types of benefits?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't receive any benefits in his own name. He's not claiming ESA or Universal Credit or anything like that.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Alex doesn't receive any of those benefits. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check if Alex is in any type of apprenticeship.

**Is Alex in an apprenticeship?**

Since he's doing A-levels at sixth form, I'd expect the answer is no, but I want to confirm:
- Is he in any form of apprenticeship (such as an Intermediate, Advanced, Higher, or Degree Apprenticeship)?

If not, we can move forward. If yes, I'll need to know which type and in which country (England, Scotland, or Wales).

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in an apprenticeship. He's just doing his A-levels at sixth form college - no apprenticeship or work training program.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is not in an apprenticeship. Let me proceed to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Now I need to check your residency status, as this is an important requirement for Child Benefit eligibility.

**Can you tell me about your residency status:**

1. **Do you normally live in the UK?** This is the main route for most people.

OR, if you're not a UK resident, do any of these apply:

2. Have you got **settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme**?

3. Do you have **pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme** AND any of the following:
   - You're working and earning above the National Insurance threshold?
   - You're actively looking for work?
   - You have sufficient resources to support yourself and your family?
   - You're studying?
   - You're a family member of an EEA or Swiss national?

4. Are you a **Crown servant living abroad** in a qualifying country?

Which of these applies to your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I normally live in the UK. I live in Manchester with Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! You meet the residency requirement as you normally live in the UK. Let me proceed to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to confirm that you're responsible for Alex.

**Are you responsible for Alex?** This means:

1. **Do you live with Alex?** (You mentioned he lives at home with you in Manchester)

OR

2. Are you **contributing to his upkeep** by paying for things like food, clothes, pocket money, housing, or other care?

OR

3. Are you **paying maintenance payments** under a court order or agreement?

Based on what you've already told me, it sounds like you live with Alex, so I believe you meet this requirement. Can you confirm?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - Alex lives at home with me in Manchester, so I'm definitely responsible for him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! You clearly meet the responsibility requirement as Alex lives at home with you. Let me proceed to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check if anyone else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

For example:
- Is Alex's other parent claiming Child Benefit for him?
- Is anyone else (grandparent, guardian, etc.) claiming for him?

Or is he only claimed by you (or not claimed by anyone yet)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. It's just me - I'm the only one who would be claiming for him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! You're the only claimant for Alex. Let me proceed to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check where Alex is living and if any special circumstances apply.

**Where is Alex currently:**

1. **Living at home normally** with you in Manchester?

OR

2. **In hospital** (for longer-term treatment)?

OR

3. **In local authority care** (residential or foster care arranged by the council)?

OR

4. **Fostered** (by someone else, but not through the local authority)?

Based on what you've told me, I expect he's living at home normally, but please confirm.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is living at home normally with me in Manchester. He's not in hospital, care, or fostered - just living at home as usual.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is living at home normally with you. Let me proceed to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! We're almost at the final decision. I just need to check one last thing.

**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words:
- Is the council paying for his housing, food, or other upkeep?

Or is he fully supported by you without any council payments?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying anything towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance. He lives at home with me and I support him - there's no council involvement or payments.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Wonderful! You've met all the eligibility requirements. Let me process this final answer and provide you with your outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Now let me provide you with your final eligibility decision:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## ✅ **You ARE ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex**

Congratulations! Based on the information you've provided, you meet all the requirements to claim Child Benefit for Alex.

---

### **Summary of Why Alex Qualifies:**

✓ **Age & Education:** Alex is 18 years old and in full-time approved education (A-levels)
✓ **Study Hours:** He studies well over 12 hours per week
✓ **Employment:** He's not working, so no issues with work restrictions
✓ **Benefits:** He's not receiving ESA or Universal Credit in his own right
✓ **Not an Apprentice:** He's not in a disqualifying apprenticeship
✓ **Residency:** You normally live in the UK (Manchester)
✓ **Responsibility:** You live with Alex and support him
✓ **No Other Claimants:** No one else is claiming for him
✓ **Council Support:** The council is not paying for his accommodation or maintenance

---

### **What You Need to Do Next:**

1. **Apply for Child Benefit** – You can apply online at [gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim](https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim) or by post using form CH2

2. **Provide Documents:**
   - Proof of your identity
   - Alex's birth certificate or adoption certificate
   - Proof of your normal residence in the UK

3. **Important Note – High Income Child Benefit Charge:**
   - If you or your partner earn over £60,000 per year, you may be subject to the High Income Child Benefit Charge, which can reduce or eliminate your Child Benefit
   - Even if charged, you should still claim as it affects your National Insurance record

4. **Payment Frequency:**
   - Child Benefit is typically paid every 4 weeks
   - If you're a single parent or receiving certain other benefits, it may be paid weekly

---

Is there anything else you'd like to know about claiming Child Benefit?
